## Overview

The Lawrence University Athletics App is an iOS application I independently designed and built as my senior capstone project. The app serves as a comprehensive records and accolades platform for Lawrence University athletics, giving users the ability to browse historical sports records and individual athlete achievements across all varsity sports.

**GitHub:** [CMSC698-Senior-Project](https://github.com/ZDoherty31/CMSC698-Senior-Project)\
**Languages & Tools:** Swift, Python, Firebase, Xcode

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What the App Does

The app has two main sides — a **user-facing side** and an **admin side**.

### User Side

-   Browse Lawrence University athletic records organized by sport
-   Search for individual players across any sport and view their personal accolades and any records they hold
-   Explore historical achievements across all varsity programs including softball, basketball, soccer, tennis, hockey, volleyball, and more

### Admin Side

-   Admins can add new records, categories, and sports directly through the app
-   Any changes made by an admin automatically update the live database in real time, keeping the app current as new records are broken

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## How I Built It

### Database Design

I built the backend using **Firebase Firestore** as the database. To populate it, I:

1.  Collected historical athletic records stored in older PDF files for each sport
2.  Converted the PDFs to JSON files
3.  Wrote Python scripts to upload the JSON data into Firebase, creating a clean, queryable database

### iOS App

The frontend is built entirely in **Swift** using Xcode. I designed the full user interface and connected it to the Firebase backend so that data loads dynamically — meaning any records added through the admin side immediately appear for all users.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Key Takeaways

This project combined several areas I care about — **sports**, **data engineering**, and **software development** — into one end-to-end application. I independently handled everything from data collection and parsing, to database design, to building and connecting the iOS frontend. It gave me hands-on experience with real-world app development challenges like parsing messy PDF data, designing a scalable database schema, and building an intuitive user interface.
